newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil bails out bankrupt Alagoas state.
newsitem.headline: Brazil bails out bankrupt Alagoas state.

text.p: The Brazilian government on Saturday agreed to bail out the bankrupt northeastern state of Alagoas, which has been driven into the ground by financial mismanagement and political cronyism, officials said.

Officials said the federal government would feed Alagoas an initial 120 million reais (about $114 million) on Aug. 15 so the state government can begin paying wages that have not been paid to its civil servants for nine months.

"If I can count on the federal government. And I can count on the political classes here, the workers, the judges, everybody, then we can find a solution," acting governor Manoel Barros told national CBN radio.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso promised Barros the emergency funds during a meeting in Rio de Janeiro.

In return, Alagoas will have to slash its swollen payroll, take away tax breaks granted powerful sugar cane distillers by former president Fernando Collor de Mello -- perhaps Alagoas' most famous son -- and drastically cut spending.
If any of those commitments are not fulfilled, Brasilia might intervene and take over the running of the state.
Barros admitted it would not be easy to save Alagoas, an impoverished state where the rule of the gun runs rife.

Under the administration of governor Divaldo Suruagy, who stepped down Thursday just as the state legislature prepared to vote on whether or not to impeach him, Alagoas had been gradually plunging deeper and deeper into financial chaos.
Suruagy has been accused by opponents of appointing at least 3,000 family members and friends to well-paid positions in the government, a charge he has not denied.

But officials in Brasilia say the origin of the state's fiscal woes lies in the decision by disgraced former president Collor, while state governor, to grant wealthy plantation owners generous tax breaks.
One of the state's most immediate problems will be what to do with its striking police force.
Unpaid for months, demonstrating police fought a gunbattle with army troops Thursday outside the legislative assembly in the capital Maceio. At least three police officers were injured.
